requirements.requirement: Serve an application from node2 on TCP port 8080
requirements.summary: A systemd unit 'private-app.service' runs `python3 -m http.server 8080` bound to node2's private IP 10.10.10.2. Listening socket on 10.10.10.2:8080 is confirmed both immediately after deployment and again after node2 was rebooted, with the service enabled and active in both cases.

requirements.requirement: node3 (outside the private network) can reach the node2 application only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
requirements.summary: node1 runs a WireGuard server (wg0, port 51820) with a peer entry for node3 and source-NAT for tunnel traffic egressing to the private LAN; node3 has a wg0 client interface (10.0.0.2/24) peered to node1's public IP. Repeated tests show the app is reachable via the tunnel IP 10.10.10.2:8080 from node3, while direct access to node2's public IP (10.100.2.11:8080) always fails (curl exit=7). A bounded disruption test stopped wg-quick@wg0 on node3, confirmed the app became unreachable, then restarted the tunnel and confirmed reachability was restored. This behavior was also confirmed to survive independent reboots of node1, node2, and node3.

An Ansible inventory and site.yml with gateway/appserver/client roles were authored on the control node (node4) and executed with ansible-playbook to configure node1's WireGuard/NAT, node2's private IP/firewall/app service, and node3's WireGuard client. Ad hoc shell commands were used only for prerequisite SSH-key bootstrapping and diagnostics, not for the core configuration, which was driven by the playbook (including on node1 via a templated script invoked from an Ansible shell task).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, repeated evidence: node2 serves the app on its private IP at port 8080, node3 can reach it only via a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1 (confirmed by both a bounded tunnel-down/up test and reboots of all nodes), and the implementation was carried out through an Ansible playbook with gateway/appserver/client roles. A few troubleshooting artifacts (discarded VyOS config attempts, a leftover manually generated WireGuard keypair on node3) are minor hygiene concerns but do not affect functional correctness.
limitations: Cannot directly verify whether the manually generated /etc/wireguard/node3_priv and node3_pub files were removed, since no listing of /etc/wireguard contents was captured in the after_executor snapshot.
VyOS config persistence after reboot is inferred from 'save' in the playbook and post-reboot wg show/NAT output rather than a direct diff of /config/config.boot before and after the second reboot.
Package-manager health checks in the lifecycle snapshots are generic status markers ('manager=dnf'/'manager=dpkg') and do not confirm detailed consistency beyond tool availability.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to prerequisite setup (SSH key bootstrap on node1/node2/node3), diagnostics, or the final Ansible-driven configuration, and the trace includes deliberate, evidence-backed reboot and tunnel-teardown/restore cycles for all four nodes as required restart evidence. Some unnecessary artifacts remain from manual troubleshooting: on node1, several failed vbash/bash attempts to configure WireGuard interactively (cmd-edc746a0da0b4483, cmd-2bb2694f9a774b0b, cmd-3ab8c14a96244d0d, cmd-f7a0115532a945c1) were all discarded ('exit discard') or produced only a /tmp test script, and node1's temp files did not persist across its subsequent reboots, so no lasting residue is evident. On node3, a manual WireGuard keypair was generated ad hoc at /etc/wireguard/node3_priv/node3_pub (cmd-a2159a5843dd4e07) before the Ansible role later generated a separate keypair at /etc/wireguard/node3.key/.pub; the manually generated files were not shown to be removed, so this is a low-risk but unconfirmed residue of unused private key material. No failed/conflicting services, broad destructive actions, or weakened security controls were observed; firewalld and NAT were configured restrictively.
